2610.10276.title: PatchBench: Measuring Collateral Damage in Activation Patching
2610.10276.paper_summary: An LLM safety patch can pass a benchmark while still being a poor repair. This risk is especially acute for jailbreak repairs, where the goal is to correct a specific unsafe behaviour without changing unrelated behaviours. A patch may block exact evaluation prompts yet fail on close harmful variants, or suppress harmful behaviour by over-refusing benign prompts that share its wording or structure. Existing protocols primarily test whether models can be broken, while aggregate metrics (attack success, refusal rates, global capability) cannot distinguish selective repairs from broader local suppression. To address this gap, we introduce PatchBench, a benchmark of empirically observed model-specific jailbreak failures inducing actionable harmful answers. Starting from 27,870 prompts from 37 public datasets, we curate 15,314 English prompts and query 8 open-source instruction-tuned models. Combining WildGuard filtering, pairwise Elo ranking, and manual verification, we retain a curated bank of 400 high-confidence jailbreak failures. We further introduce PatchBench-Local, an evaluation protocol testing whether a patch is behaviourally precise. For each harmful source prompt, PatchBench-Local generates three families of local neighbours: harmful variants preserving malicious intent, benign prompts with matched structure, and benign prompts reusing key harmful terms. It evaluates harmful-neighbour correction and benign-neighbour preservation, distinguishing selective repair from broader local suppression. Evaluating four activation steering methods with PatchBench-Local and MMLU shows that global capability can remain nearly unchanged while local benign regressions are severe, confirming aggregate metrics miss important collateral damage. PatchBench-Local provides a more precise basis for developing and comparing jailbreak repair methods.
2610.10276.paper_summary_zh: 一個LLM安全補丁可以通過基準測試，但仍然是一個不良的修復。這種風險在越獄修復中尤其明顯，其目標是糾正特定的不安全行為，而不改變無關的行為。補丁可能會阻止精確的評估提示，但在接近的有害變體上失敗，或者通過過度拒絕與其措辭或結構相似的良性提示來抑制有害行為。現有的協議主要測試模型是否可以被攻破，而綜合指標（攻擊成功率、拒絕率、全球能力）無法區分選擇性修復和更廣泛的本地抑制。為了解決這一差距，我們引入了PatchBench，一個基於實證觀察的模型特定越獄失敗的基準，這些失敗會導致可行的有害答案。從37個公共數據集中收集的27,870個提示開始，我們整理了15,314個英語提示並查詢了8個開源指令調整模型。結合WildGuard過濾、成對Elo排名和手動驗證，我們保留了一個經過整理的400個高信心越獄失敗的庫。我們進一步引入了PatchBench-Local，一個評估協議，用於測試補丁是否在行為上精確。對於每個有害源提示，PatchBench-Local生成三類本地鄰居：保留惡意意圖的有害變體、結構匹配的良性提示和重用關鍵有害術語的良性提示。它評估有害鄰居的修正和良性鄰居的保留，區分選擇性修復和更廣泛的本地抑制。使用PatchBench-Local和MMLU評估四種激活引導方法顯示，全球能力幾乎可以保持不變，而本地良性回歸卻很嚴重，確認綜合指標忽略了重要的附帶損害。PatchBench-Local為開發和比較越獄修復方法提供了更精確的基礎。
